title: How Much Fiber in Brussels Sprouts? 4.1g per Cup
description: Brussels Sprouts: about 4.1 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (14% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in Brussels sprouts?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Brussels sprouts, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

intro: Brussels sprouts rank #6 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in brussels sprouts by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in Brussels sprouts?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists brussels sprouts, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt at 2.6 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 156 g) therefore has about 4.1 g of fiber and 56 calories. That is 14% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 16% of a 25 g day and 11% of a 38 g day.
Brussels sprouts are dense little cabbages, so a cup holds more fiber than a cup of leafy greens. Roasting has made them one of the more popular high-fiber side dishes.

sections.heading: Roasted, shaved, or boiled
paragraphs: Roasting and boiling do not change the fiber much; shredding them raw into a salad gives a lighter, lower-fiber cup because it is less tightly packed.
Like other cruciferous vegetables, Brussels sprouts can cause gas for some people. Smaller portions more often tend to work better than one large serving.

sections.heading: How Brussels sprouts compare with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, Brussels sprouts rank #6 for fiber per typical serving and #7 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 7.2 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [green beans](/fiber-in-green-beans) at 4 g (1 cup, cooked); [baked potato](/fiber-in-potato) at 3.8 g (1 medium, baked, flesh and skin); [spinach](/fiber-in-spinach) at 4.3 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), Brussels sprouts are #12 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding Brussels sprouts to your day
paragraphs: Roast halved sprouts with olive oil until browned, then toss with a little balsamic or mustard. A cup alongside beans or whole grains makes a high-fiber dinner.

Example: 1 cup brussels sprouts, 1 cup quinoa, 1/2 cup chickpeas. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 15.5 g of fiber, with 4.1 g from the Brussels sprouts. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of Brussels sprouts?
faqs.a: 2.6 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Brussels sprouts, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in Brussels sprouts (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 2 g, for 78 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Are Brussels sprouts higher in fiber than broccoli?
faqs.a: Close. Cooked Brussels sprouts are about 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked); cooked broccoli is about 5.1 g (1 cup chopped, cooked).

faqs.q: Why do Brussels sprouts cause gas?
faqs.a: They contain fermentable carbohydrates and sulfur compounds. Building up gradually usually helps.
